title: pvClip
body:
## pvClip

Full native Clip: cuts the input with an implicit function chosen in ClipType (Plane, Box, Sphere, Cylinder) or with a scalar iso-value (ClipType Scalar plus Scalars and Value) and keeps one side, returning an unstructured grid. Crinkleclip keeps whole cells instead of cutting them. HyperTreeGridClipper replaces ClipType for hyper-tree-grid input. Use clip for a simple plane clip with Schemaxis defaults.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- ParaView starts with Invert true, which keeps the region inside the function (behind a plane's normal, inside a sphere or box); set Invert false to keep the other side.
- With ClipType Scalar, point arrays are clipped exactly at Value, while cell arrays remove whole cells (threshold-like).
- Schemaxis ships a Plane clip example (examples/schemaxis/paraview-catalogue.json), but the operation's coverage records no native qualification run; other clip types are unexercised.

Native constructor: `Clip`. Identity: `filters/Clip`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the dataset on which the Clip filter will operate. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType` | This property specifies the parameters of the clip function (an implicit description) used to clip the dataset. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Box","Cylinder","Plane","Scalar","Sphere"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Box"}` |
| `Crinkleclip` | This parameter controls whether to extract entire cells in the given region or clip those cells so all of the output will stay only on that side of region. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Exact` | If this property is set to 1 it will clip to the exact specifications for the **Box** option only, otherwise the clip will only approximate the box geometry. The exact clip is very expensive as it requires generating 6 plane clips. Additionally, **Invert** must be checked and **Crinkle clip** must be unchecked. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper` | This property specifies the parameters of the clip function (an implicit description) used to clip the hyper tree grid. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Axis Aligned Box","Cylinder","Plane","Scalar","Sphere"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Axis Aligned Box"}` |
| `Invert` | Invert which part of the geometry is clipped. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Scalars` | If clipping with scalars, this property specifies the name of the scalar array on which to perform the clip operation. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `UseValueAsOffset` | If UseValueAsOffset is true, Value is used as an offset parameter to the implicit function. Otherwise, Value is used only when clipping using a scalar array. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Value` | If clipping with scalars, this property sets the scalar value about which to clip the dataset based on the scalar array chosen. (See SelectInputScalars.) If clipping with a clip function, this property specifies an offset from the clip function to use in the clipping operation. Neither functionality is currently available in ParaView's user interface. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `Box`

Syntax: `{"type":"Box","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Box`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Bounds` | Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Length` | With UseReferenceBounds false: edge lengths [Lx, Ly, Lz] of the box along its own axes (ParaView applies them as scale factors to a unit cube). With UseReferenceBounds true: dimensionless scale factors applied to the Bounds box about the coordinate origin. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Position` | With UseReferenceBounds false: world coordinates [x, y, z] of the box’s minimum corner (before rotation); the box extends from Position to Position + Length along its own axes. With UseReferenceBounds true: a translation applied to the transformed Bounds box. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Rotation` | Rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] about the x, y and z axes, applied about the box’s local origin (its minimum corner at Position, not its centre; with UseReferenceBounds true, about the coordinate origin). The angles are combined in VTK’s Z-X-Y convention: the box transform is Translate · RotateZ · RotateX · RotateY · Scale. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.UseReferenceBounds` | Chooses how the box is defined. False: the box is a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated about its corner and placed at Position. True: the box starts from Bounds, and Length, Rotation and Position act as scale, rotation and translation relative to it (about the coordinate origin). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `Cylinder`

Syntax: `{"type":"Cylinder","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Cylinder`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Axis` | Direction [ax, ay, az] of the cylinder's axis line through Center; the cylinder is infinitely long in both directions. For ordinary datasets ParaView normalizes the vector, so only its direction matters. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Center` | Any point [x, y, z] on the cylinder’s axis line. Moving it along Axis changes nothing; moving it sideways moves the cylinder. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Radius` | Distance from the axis line to the cylinder surface; points closer than this are inside. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ClipType.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `Scalar`

Syntax: `{"type":"Scalar","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Scalar`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

No authored options.


### Nested `ClipType` → `Sphere`

Syntax: `{"type":"Sphere","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Sphere`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Center` | Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere in the input’s coordinates; the region within Radius of this point is inside. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Radius` | Radius of the sphere: points closer than Radius to Center are inside. A larger radius encloses more of the data or moves the cut shell outward. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `HyperTreeGridClipper` → `Axis Aligned Box`

Syntax: `{"type":"Axis Aligned Box","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Axis Aligned Box`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper.options.Bounds` | Native reference bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]. The hyper-tree-grid clip computes its box from Position and Length, so Bounds does not affect the result. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper.options.Length` | Edge lengths [Lx, Ly, Lz] of the clipping box; the far corner is Position + Length. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper.options.Position` | Minimum corner [x, y, z] of the clipping box; the box spans Position to Position + Length on each axis. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper.options.Rotation` | Native box orientation angles. The hyper-tree-grid clip that uses this choice builds its box from Position and Length only, so Rotation has no effect on the result. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `HyperTreeGridClipper.options.UseReferenceBounds` | Native switch that makes a ParaView box relative to Bounds. The hyper-tree-grid clip reads Position and Length directly, so this switch does not change its result. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvClip",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
